reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address FeNiCrCoCu coatings, grain refinement by cooling rate, high-temperature sliding wear, or oxide layer formation. E1 uses ML/MD for tension-compression asymmetry, and E2 studies a different HEA system (FeCoCrNiAlWx) with W addition, not grain size effects. Thus, none of the key premises are supported by the provided passages.
premises: Grain refinement in FeNiCrCoCu HEA coatings can be achieved by enhanced cooling rate during deposition.
Grain refinement increases microhardness in this HEA system.
Grain boundaries act as effective barriers to dislocation motion at high temperature.
A refined grain structure promotes the formation of a stable, protective oxide layer during high-temperature sliding.
Increased microhardness and a stable oxide layer reduce wear rate and plastic deformation.
